subject: Nebula Labs Dedicated Commit — phased onramp & milestone credits
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Choi <sara.choi@nebulalabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Phased GPU commit proposal + term sheet (draft)

Sara —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation attached is a starting point for a multi-year dedicated commit that tries to balance Nebula's desire to accelerate GPU capacity in year one with Redwood's need for predictable ramp economics. The two attachments are: capacity_ramp_table.xlsx (proposed phased commits by quarter) and Draft_Term_Sheet_Nebula_v3.pdf (commercial terms).

Key highlights:
- Baseline reserved pool expressed as TPM-equivalent and GPU slots; baseline priced at a blended rate.
- Phased onramp over 12 months: 30% of final committed GPU pool available in Q1, 60% by end of Q3, 100% by EOY.
- Term: 3 years (annual prepay option available); we surfaced a 7% term discount on prepay vs. annual billing in the draft.
- SLA credit framework: automatic credits for missed latency/availability SLOs (draft figures in term sheet).

Open items I want to highlight up front:
1) You mentioned wanting faster access to burst capacity for training windows; we can carve a burst pool but it comes at different utilization economics.
2) If you prefer a steeper ramp, we can restructure year 1 prepay mix but that will affect the overall discount curve.
3) DocuSign-ready term sheet once we land on final numbers — I included a placeholder in the related links.

Would you be able to review and call out the three top commercial changes you need by Thursday? If helpful, Karthik can put together a short runbook showing how baseline vs. burst maps to your workloads.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Draft_Term_Sheet_Nebula_v3.pdf (pdf), capacity_ramp_table.xlsx (xls)
From: Sara Choi <sara.choi@nebulalabs.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nebulalabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased GPU commit proposal + term sheet (draft)

Laura —

Thanks for the draft and the clear summary. Quick feedback after an internal sync:

1) Ramp speed — Nebula is willing to commit long-term but needs a faster Year-1 onramp. Can we move to 50% of the full committed pool by end of Q2 (instead of 30% in Q1)? That lets us get prod traffic onto dedicated GPUs sooner.

2) Discount curve — the 7% prepay uplift is okay, but because we're committing for 3 years we want an indexed step-up discount in year 3 (an additional 3–5% deeper discount if we hit minimum utilization thresholds).

3) SLA credits — the concept is fine but we need stronger recourse for repeated misses (not just credits): a right to a one-time additional credit or temporary increase to burst capacity if we have two missed quarters in a 12-month window.

4) Burst capacity — yes, we need burst for scheduled training. What's the pricing delta and can burst be capped as a percentage of baseline?

We're looping in procurement (Tom) for the contract-side items. If you can send an updated ramp table with the 50% by Q2 option and a short commercial counter that calls out how the discount would move if we add the year-3 utilization kicker, that will get us to procurement review faster.

Sara
Head of Platform, Nebula Labs
sara.choi@nebulalabs.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Choi <sara.choi@nebulalabs.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased GPU commit proposal + term sheet (draft)

Sara / Laura —

Quick technical note to make the commercial discussion more concrete:

- We can split capacity into a Baseline pool (reserved, low-latency, guaranteed KV cache residency) and a Burst pool (preemptible pricing tier; higher per-token cost but available on-demand).
- Suggested structure: baseline = 85% of each committed GPU's guaranteed throughput; burst = up to 40% additional throughput available for scheduled windows. Burst would be billed at ~1.8x baseline per-token economics in the draft.
- For the 50% by Q2 ramp ask: operationally feasible if we accept a staged GPU activation fee and a small upfront increase in Year-1 prepay (we can model this explicitly).

I've attached a short extract from our SLA pack that defines the credit calculation and the hit thresholds — see redwood-sla-extract.pdf. If Nebula wants a stronger non-credit remediation (temporary burst increase), we can bake in a single remedial burst window per 12-month period tied to repeat SLA misses.

Happy to walk through with a quick screen-share.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-sla-extract.pdf
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Choi <sara.choi@nebulalabs.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@nebulalabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 10:14:00 -0700
Subject: NW: Commercial counter — faster Year-1 onramp + conditional year-3 kicker

Team —

Thanks for the detailed asks — appreciate the clarity. Below is our commercial counter to the points you raised. I'm putting the numbers here so procurement has a single place to review before we produce an updated term sheet.

Committed proposal (counter):
- Term: 3 years, annual prepay with optional multi-year invoicing. Deal ID: NB-2026-0417.
- Onramp: 50% of final committed pool available by end of Q2 (operational activation schedule attached). 80% by end of Q3, 100% by end of Q4.
- Pricing/discounts: base prepay discount = 9% off list for the 3-year annual-prepay profile. If Nebula achieves utilization >= 85% across the committed baseline for any rolling 12-month period in Year 3, Redwood will provide an additional 4% rebate applied to Year 3 charges (the "Year-3 Utilization Kicker").
- Burst: configurable burst pool up to 40% of baseline throughput. Burst rate = 1.75x baseline token price. Burst is subject to a monthly cap (suggested 20% of baseline consumption) unless otherwise negotiated.
- SLA remediation: automatic credit schedule remains per SLA doc. For repeated SLA misses (defined as 2 missed quarterly SLOs in a trailing 12-month window), Redwood will grant either a one-time credit equal to 8% of the affected quarter's baseline charges or a single remedial burst window (up to 72 hours) at no additional charge.
- Activation fee & Year-1 mechanics: to support the accelerated 50% by Q2 ramp, we propose a one-time activation fee equal to 1.5% of Year-1 committed spend; this can be credited back if Nebula extends beyond Year-2 or exceeds baseline utilization thresholds.

Next steps:
1) If this framework looks acceptable, we'll issue Rev 4 of the term sheet and an updated capacity_ramp_table.xlsx reflecting the 50% by Q2 schedule.
2) We will include the Year-3 utilization kicker language and the remedial burst option in the commercial annex.
3) We'll prepare a DocuSign envelope for procurement (link in related_links).

Marissa (CS lead) and Jonas (dedicated ops) are looped in to confirm operational readiness for the faster ramp and the remedial burst process.

Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Date: Sun, 24 May 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NW: Commercial counter — faster Year-1 onramp + conditional year-3 kicker

Laura —

Thanks — this is much closer to what we need. A couple of minor asks before procurement signs:

1) Can the Year-3 kicker be measured on a 12-month trailing basis ending on the anniversary date rather than any rolling 12 months? That aligns with our internal reporting cadence.
2) For the remedial burst window, can you add a clause that the remedial window is not usable within the first 90 days post-activation to avoid edge cases during the initial ramp?

If you can accept those two changes, we'll get procurement to review Rev 4 and aim to sign within 5 business days.
